Flow & Ergonomics

Direction parity, wrist comfort, travel, and two-hand collision penalties.

Two simultaneous notes for every detected onset, with independently planned long-flow sequences and a joint two-saber geometry solver. Enabled by default.

Audio-derived long sections, independently timed left/right patterns, repeated motifs and joint swing simulation. Keeps the existing beat detector unchanged.

Similarity for repeated long musical sections, based on 12 time-resampled acoustic/rhythm bins. 0.83 default.

Strength of long top/bottom alternations, orbital loops, diagonals and waves. 0 uses mostly mined corpus sequences; 0.9 balanced.

Explore more of the 121K human-mined flows across different sections. Repeated musical phrases still share their patterns; unsafe transitions are rejected. 0 = conservative, 0.85 = diverse.

Prefer roughly equal bottom, middle, and upper-row note counts. Balances across the song and nearby phrases without changing beat times or bypassing wrist and collision safety. 0 = original distribution, 1.3 = balanced.

Only used when full double-note mode is OFF; controls occasional shared accents in single-hand rhythmic mode.

Use real 3–10 note human-mined patterns with a wrist/hand safety simulation. Keeps current beat detection unchanged.

Minimum acoustic/rhythmic similarity to reuse the same full flow. Higher avoids false matches.

1.0 balanced; 1.2 stricter parity, arm reach, and strain constraints. Simulated, not a medical guarantee.
